title: Anaphoric Annotation in the ARRAU Corpus
research_question: Can an anaphora annotation scheme represent ambiguous interpretations, multiple antecedents, and discourse deixis to abstract clause-level antecedents with useful human agreement across dialogue and written genres?
methodology: The authors developed ARRAU through a series of annotation experiments, often using MMAX2, in which multiple annotators independently marked anaphoric phenomena and agreement was assessed with measures including Krippendorff's alpha. The resulting corpus combines task-oriented TRAINS dialogues, Pear Stories, GNOME texts, and Wall Street Journal material; noun phrases are markables and clauses can serve as potential antecedents for discourse deixis. The scheme uses pointers from anaphoric expressions to antecedents, permits multiple pointers for plural antecedents, separate pointer sets for ambiguous interpretations, and pointers from referring noun phrases to clauses introducing events, actions, or plans. The paper reports corpus composition and summarizes preliminary use of the annotations in anaphora-resolution experiments.

key_findings.finding: Agreement on anaphoric chains in the reported annotation experiments was approximately alpha 0.6-0.7.
key_findings.section: 3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis

key_findings.finding: For discourse deixis, annotators tended to agree on the general antecedent region but disagreed about exact boundaries, yielding agreement around alpha 0.55.
key_findings.section: 3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis

key_findings.finding: The annotation experiments motivated constraining discourse-deixis antecedent regions to predefined clause-level units and distinguishing plural multi-antecedent cases from genuinely ambiguous alternative interpretations.
key_findings.section: 3 Agreement on ambiguity and discourse deixis

key_findings.finding: The reported corpus contains 110 texts and 94,212 words, including 455 markables pointing to textual regions and 103 explicitly ambiguous markables.
ARRAU can encode several antecedents for a plural anaphoric expression and can encode two alternative sets of antecedent pointers for ambiguity.
Reference to an abstract event, action, or plan is represented by linking the referring noun phrase to the clause introducing that abstract entity.

The paper does not annotate conversational reply-to relations, proposition-level answer scope, unanswered subquestions, or scoped approval and rejection; its multiple-antecedent mechanism concerns anaphoric reference rather than a response jointly answering multiple propositions.

limitations: Human agreement is only moderate for anaphoric chains and lower for the exact boundaries of discourse-deictic antecedents, showing that scope annotation is intrinsically difficult.
The corpus contains task-oriented dialogue but is not a workplace-email or enterprise-messaging corpus.
Clause-level discourse-deixis antecedents identify what an anaphoric expression refers to; they do not encode which prior questions or propositions a reply answers.

Multiple antecedent pointers principally represent plural reference, while separate pointer sets represent ambiguity, so they should not be interpreted as empirical evidence about one reply jointly responding to several propositions.
The preliminary system experiment converted richer pointer structures into equivalence sets and selected the first interpretation for ambiguous anaphors, losing some of the annotation's complexity.

At the time described by the paper, a first corpus release had been completed and used in a workshop, but the paper only states an intention to make the corpus publicly available before LREC, so public dataset availability is not established by this source.
The paper summarizes agreement results partly from earlier experiments rather than reporting a fresh comprehensive reliability analysis for every corpus genre.
raw_claims: ARRAU was designed to cover ambiguous anaphoric expressions and references to abstract entities.
Its genres include TRAINS task-oriented dialogue as well as narrative and written text.
As many as twenty annotators participated independently in some annotation experiments.
Anaphoric-chain agreement was reported in roughly the 0.6-0.7 alpha range.
Discourse-deixis antecedent boundaries produced agreement of about 0.55 alpha.
All clauses are treated as potential antecedents for discourse deixis.
Multiple pointers from one expression can encode plural antecedents.
Two distinct pointer sets can encode alternative interpretations of an ambiguous expression.
An event, action, or plan reference can point from a noun phrase to the clause introducing the abstract entity.
Table 1 reports 110 texts and 94,212 words in the corpus.
The annotation scheme does not define a question-answer completeness or partial-reply relation.
